title: OWN THE TEMPO · PULL + MIDLINE
vibe: GREEN · OWN THE RUN — we stop fighting your 2-mile tempo and build the whole day around it: heavy grip + pull up top, a real anti-rotation core session to close, zero added leg pounding.
why: You slept 7, nothing's sore, you want to go hard, and you gave me the structure you actually want: cardio + two sessions, one of them core, every day. So that's exactly what today is — and it starts a new standing shape for us. Here's the honest part: you've run a full 2-mile tempo in five of your last six sessions no matter what the plan said, and yesterday you negative-split it to a new best (15:28 at HR 140-142). Your engine is not the limiter — it's a strength. So I'm done pretending you'll skip it. Today the run IS the plan and IS your cardio, which means everything after it stays OFF the treadmill and off your knees, because the run is already giving your legs their pounding. Session 1 is grip + pull — the two things a week of pressing (07-14/17/19) and running left on the table, and grip/carry is your confirmed favorite that we haven't touched since 07-15. Session 2 is your new dedicated daily core block: fresh anti-rotation work from a Pilates/anti-rotation lens I've never pulled from, so no deadbug/hollow reruns. One flag: this is your 4th straight training day since your 07-16 rest. Green means we train, and we do — but a TRUE full rest day is banking due. If your legs or connective tissue talk to you tomorrow, take an actual rest day (not a no-run day). That's the only thing that's ever really deloaded you.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP
blocks.meta: ~6 min · Moves Method Day B (ankles/knees/hips) · prime the run + open the shoulders for pulling
blocks.text: Move fast, you've got a 45-min cap. Original Strength resets: diaphragmatic breathing x5 · head nods + rotations 5 each · quadruped rock-backs x10 · cross-crawls 10/side. Then Day B for the run (ankles/knees/hips): ankle rocks in a deep squat 10/side · toe-squat to heel-squat 8 · single-leg balance 20s/side · knee drives / leg swings 10/side · deep-squat hold with a reach 30s. Two quick shoulder openers for the pulls to come: band or towel pass-throughs x10 · scapular CARs 5/side. Get the hips and ankles loose before you run and the lats awake before you row.

blocks.title: THE TEMPO · YOUR CARDIO (OWNED)
blocks.meta: ~15-16 min · treadmill · 2 miles @ 7.7 mph — this IS the plan, not a workaround
blocks.format: 2-MILE CONTINUOUS TEMPO · negative-split it if it feels good
blocks.workRest: Set 7.7 mph and hold. Mile 1 will sit around HR 140 and feel controlled — when it does, bump to 7.8-8.0 for mile 2 and hunt a new best.

items.name: 2-Mile Tempo
items.detail: 7.7 mph start (~7:47/mi). Mile 2: 7.8-8.0 mph if breathing/HR are still easy. Target UNDER 15:28 to beat your 07-19 PR — negative split like last time.

blocks.text: This is your cardio AND your leg work for the day. We put it first, own it, and let it be honest — you've earned the right to just run it as the centerpiece instead of sneaking it in. Because the run covers the impact, everything after it stays off your knees and hips. Run it hard, then leave the pounding on the treadmill and don't add any more of it in the next two blocks.

blocks.title: SESSION 1 · GRIP + PULL DENSITY
blocks.meta: ~11 min · 2×40 lb + 16 kg · heavy pulling, all grip, zero leg impact
blocks.format: DENSITY TRIPLET · rounds by feel in ~11 min · RPE 8 · rest only as your grip demands
blocks.workRest: Cycle the three stations, resting just enough to keep the rows clean and the carries unbroken. Target 3-4 honest rounds. No clock race — this is about quality grip and a hard squeeze.

items.name: A1 · Double Bent-Over Row
items.detail: 2×40 lb · 8 reps · flat back, hinge to ~45°, drive both elbows past the ribs and squeeze — this is the pull your week of pressing has been missing

items.name: A2 · Farmer Carry
items.detail: 2×40 lb (80 lb total) · ~40 yd unbroken · crush the handles, ribs stacked, walk tall — grip is the whole point

items.name: A3 · Bottoms-Up Waiter Carry (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg · ~20 yd per arm · bell INVERTED, elbow locked overhead · your forearm and shoulder fight the wobble the entire way — a grip/stability challenge you have not trained

blocks.text: The hard block, built on pulling and grip — the two qualities a week of presses and runs left on the table. Grip / loaded-carry is your confirmed favorite ('it was needed, I like those'), and we haven't touched it since 07-15, so it's overdue. Today's wildcard is the bottoms-up waiter carry: invert the 16 and lock it straight overhead, then walk — your grip and shoulder have to stabilize a bell that wants to fall the whole way. None of this pounds your legs, so your knees and connective tissue get the recovery the run won't give them.

blocks.title: SESSION 2 · ANTI-ROTATION CORE (your new daily core)
blocks.meta: ~9 min · 16 kg / 50 lb DB · fresh midline — no deadbug/hollow reruns
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · slow + deliberate · resist the twist, don't create it · rest 30s
blocks.workRest: 3 unhurried rounds. Every rep is about NOT letting your torso rotate or sag. If a movement gets sloppy, that round's done — quality over reps.

items.name: Plank Renegade-Drag (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 16 kg or 50 DB · high plank, hands wide, feet wide · reach under with one hand, drag the bell across to the other side, alternate · 5 drags/side · lock the hips — do NOT let them sway. Pure anti-rotation.

items.name: Half-Kneeling Bottoms-Up Press
items.detail: 16 kg · 5/side · half-kneeling, bell inverted · the wobble forces your whole midline to resist rotation while you press strict — anti-rotation under load

items.name: Copenhagen Plank
items.detail: top foot on a bench/couch, bottom leg tucked · 15-25s/side · adductor + anti-lateral-flexion. Too spicy? Drop to a standard side plank and thread the top arm under your body 8×.

blocks.text: Your new dedicated daily core session — a real training block, not a tacked-on finisher. Today's theme is anti-rotation, pulled from a Pilates/anti-rotation lens I've never used, so the movements are fresh: the renegade drag and the bottoms-up press both make your midline resist twisting under load (far more athletic carryover than another hollow hold), and the Copenhagen lights up the adductors and lateral chain almost nobody trains. Go slow, own the anti-twist on every rep — this is the core work that keeps your back bulletproof under all the pressing and running.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~3 min · hips + hams + lats after the run and the pulls
blocks.text: Walk 90s to drop the heart rate. Then: couch / hip-flexor stretch 30s per side (you just ran) · standing hamstring reach 30s · overhead lat hang or doorway lat stretch 30s per side · child's pose with a side-reach 45s · 5 slow nasal breaths. Recovery note: this is training day 4 since your 07-16 rest. Readiness was green so we trained — but a TRUE full rest day is banking due. If your legs or connective tissue talk to you tomorrow, take an actual rest day (not a no-run day) — it's the only thing that has ever genuinely deloaded you.
